476.t: Leaving Desdunes a month before the break-up
476.s: Harry left a month before the band folded as money got short and men missed their families; Desmond took his place.
476.q: I think that was Desmond or something, wanted to make some money. I don't know. The band was going, was about to break up.

767.t: Own band in Temple, then joining Walter Wardell and Boots in San Antonio
767.s: Steering toward the Wild Cherry record, Harris tells how he led a band in Temple, was recruited by Boots and Walter Wardell for San Antonio, and stayed until the band broke up over money.
767.ch: Boots and His Buddies and Wild Cherry
767.q: I'll play with it. Well then I came out on the house and came on down here and organized a band again in Temple, Texas. I stayed there and while I was there Boots had played with me in Houston and he heard that I was in Temple and Walter Wardell was here organizing the band. Boots told him, I know…

406.t: Leaving the Cotton Pickers: the fight over Billy Borne's clarinet
406.s: When he gave notice, the Cotton Pickers refused his pay; he took Billy Borne's clarinet and a brawl followed. Cab lent him $100, and Barefield impressed him by writing arrangements overnight.
406.ch: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
406.q: Pickers my notice that I was going with Cab Calloway and they all got mad. And I was using Billy Borne's clarinet and so they --

1.t: Social Security deduction and quitting on toilet paper
1.s: Danny argued with the band's manager Steve over a twenty-five dollar Social Security deduction and handed in notice on toilet paper.
1.ch: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
1.q: So we go to Boston, and we worked there a week. When we get paid...I can't think of the guy... Steve, who was the head of the Savoy; he runs the management. When we get paid, it's supposed to be... Payday is Sunday night, but you have to go there Monday. He gets the check, and he goes there to cash…

87.t: Why the band broke up: pay, road and buses
87.s: Pay and the hard road led men to leave; the band held a meeting at the Harlem YMCA about leaking buses.
87.q: Well, that was partly -- one of the reasons. I had misgivings about leaving it because I enjoyed playing with the guys in the band. At the same time when I was leaving it, other guys were leaving it too, Willie Smith and -- he had left it -- and Sy left first, going right for Tommy Dorsey.

67.t: The Cotton Pickers break up in Detroit over unpaid wages
67.s: Because the band was not being paid, the bass player hid the music and demanded his back pay, and the band broke up in Detroit.
67.q: And so bass player was the first to leave, so he took all -- somehow or other he got hold to the music. He took all the music and hid it. So we didn't have anything -- we could've faked, but McKinney wanted his music. That was why the band broke up and this bass player kept the music and called Mac…

69.t: Leaving Duke for Harry James in 1944
69.s: Duke refused to loan $3,000 for his house, so Tizol quit, with Harry James offering a good salary and his base in California.
69.ch: Harry James, Bellson and the return to Duke
69.q: the Cotton Club, and I asked Duke to give me some money to pay for the home, the balance on my home, which was about $3,000 owed on the home. I said, "Would you loan me that money and take it out of my salary?" Oh, he swore that he didn't have the money, and this and the other and so forth, and at…

19.t: Quitting Jacquet over money in September 1948
19.s: A pay controversy with Jacquet, partly his own headstrong youth, makes him leave and return to Washington.
19.ch: Trio, Eckstine accompanist and Illinois Jacquet, 1945-48
19.q: Of course, after Jo left, for some reason.... I hope I'm not getting ahead of myself in this situation... Anyway, I think Jo stayed there until I left, and I left in 1948 -- I think it was another September that I left. And it had to do with a little controversy again that had to do with the money…

389.t: Fired when Whiteman cut the band to sixteen pieces
389.s: Whiteman told him he was fired as he downsized, and eight men left together.
389.q: Yeah, well, you know, then he says, "I'm sorry, but I'm going to have to cut the band down, the way things are going now, he says we can't keep the big band.

75.t: The Rex Stewart band tours and breaks up
75.s: The band lasted a year or two, toured Baltimore and Washington with Chauncey Houghton, then broke up amid transportation and booking troubles.
75.ch: Early 1930s: Bessie Smith, Rex Stewart and the Harlem scene
75.q: Because it was...Chauncey Houghton from Baltimore later joined the band, and we went on a tour. We played the Lafayette, then we went on tour to Baltimore, Washington, D.C., places like that. Then the band broke up.
